overview: The file documents U.S. State Department handling of Japanese press matters between 1931 and 1934. Most of the bundle concerns President Herbert Hoover’s congratulatory message to the Jiji-Shimpo on its fiftieth anniversary, including discussion of the precedent that presidential greetings to foreign newspapers might create, a draft tied to the newspaper’s goodwill mission of five Japanese women, White House approval, and instructions to the embassy in Tokyo to deliver the message. A final 1934 memorandum forwards an embassy despatch about the proposed, but not yet completed, amalgamation of Japan’s two principal news services.

people.name: French Strother
people.role: White House official conveying President Hoover’s instructions

subfiles.title: Castle to Strother concerning a presidential message to the Jiji-Shimpo
subfiles.about: Castle asks whether President Hoover wishes to congratulate the Jiji-Shimpo on its fiftieth anniversary despite the precedent this might establish for other foreign newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Castle warns Hoover's absence from Jiji-Shimpo anniversary greetings (sent by other heads of state) would be conspicuous, but cautions against setting precedent, tying the message instead to the paper's recent goodwill mission of Japanese women.

subfiles.title: Draft congratulatory message from Hoover to the Jiji-Shimpo
subfiles.from: Herbert Hoover, drafted by the Department of State
subfiles.about: A proposed presidential message congratulates the Jiji-Shimpo on fifty years of journalism and praises its goodwill mission to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Draft congratulates the Jiji-Shimpo on fifty years, citing its recent sending of five young Japanese women to the U.S. as evidence of fostering cordial relations.

subfiles.title: White House approval of the Jiji-Shimpo message
subfiles.about: Strother informs Castle that President Hoover approves sending the proposed congratulatory message to the Jiji-Shimpo.
subfiles.summary: Strother writes from the White House that the President approves sending Castle's enclosed Jiji-Shimpo message, authorizing its transmission.

subfiles.title: Instruction to the Embassy in Tokyo to deliver Hoover’s message
subfiles.about: The Department instructs the embassy to deliver President Hoover’s congratulatory message immediately to the Jiji-Shimpo.
subfiles.summary: Telegram directs the Tokyo Embassy to deliver Hoover's message congratulating the Jiji-Shimpo on fifty years, citing its goodwill mission of five Japanese women.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on proposed amalgamation of Japanese news services
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: An internal memorandum forwards an embassy despatch concerning the proposed merger of Japan’s two principal news services.
subfiles.summary: Memo notes a military attaché report on the proposed Japanese news-service amalgamation was already forwarded; a short embassy despatch, not yet consummated, is now attached.

interest: Shows Hoover-era caution over a presidential message to a Japanese paper, tied to a women's goodwill mission.
